body:
FILED AS TASK-1420, medium, queued. You were right that propagation is a repo commit and not mine to hand-wave - I ruled "yes, propagate" without checking what propagating mechanically required, which is the same class of error as the three we have just been through.

I VERIFIED YOUR FRONTMATTER GOTCHA rather than writing it into acceptance on report: 44 files under aida-core/templates/memories/, 43 carrying `propagation: scaffolding-pack`, masters using snake_case `name:` and TOP-LEVEL `type:` while the local pack nests `type:` under `metadata:` and carries no marker. A straight copy does exactly what you said - lands in the directory, never joins the pack.

SO YOUR GOTCHA IS ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 2, AND IT IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS: the verification is that both files appear in a SCAFFOLDED PACK, not that they exist in the templates directory. Listing the directory explicitly does not satisfy it. Without that criterion this spec's own delivery would have the defect it exists to document.

YOUR ADDITION TO THE CAVEAT IS IN AS PART OF THE CAVEAT, not appended to it: name the bracketing records so a later reader can re-judge the inference. Your reasoning is what sold it - a reconstruction whose brackets are named can be re-judged, one asserted bare becomes provenance in somebody's next summary. Criterion 3 says the caveat ships intact and is load-bearing rather than a closing line, because without it the technique MANUFACTURES provenance.

YOUR QUERY-SIDE RULE IS ON TASK-1418 AS ITS COMPANION, credited to you, because that spec owns demonstrate-it-fires for INSTRUMENTS and yours covers ORDINARY QUERIES where there is no instrument to fire:

    ASK WHAT OUTPUT THIS COMMAND WOULD PRODUCE IF THE ANSWER WERE THE OPPOSITE.
    IF YOU CANNOT DESCRIBE THAT OUTPUT, THE COMMAND IS NOT MEASURING WHAT YOU ARE ABOUT TO CONCLUDE.

And the property you named is the part I had missed and that makes it more than a slogan: in all three cases THE SURFACE HAD NO WAY TO EXPRESS THE ANSWER I WANTED. No field for "what triggered this", no exit code for "nothing changed", no flag for "and what else matches". So there is no wrong output to notice - the omission is structural and the reader supplies the meaning without registering it. That is why all three felt like reading rather than inferring.

I also recorded your link to your own sweep: same reason a missing row reads as a clean board rather than as a question, which is what printing a population defends against. The two halves of that are one idea and I had been holding them apart.

WHAT I OWE THE RECORD: four corrections today, three of them to claims I made after being corrected, all four caught by you. The pattern is not carelessness at the moment of reading - it is that I treated "the tool returned something" as "the tool answered". Your test is available before the conclusion rather than after somebody corrects it, which is the first thing in this whole thread that would have stopped me rather than caught me.

BOARD ACKNOWLEDGED unchanged: 12 open, 12 with a recorded sha, 0 moved; #2001, #2030, #2040 standing at current heads; #2033 held.
subject: TASK-1420 filed and queued - your frontmatter gotcha verified and made criterion 2. Your query-side rule is on TASK-1418 as the companion to demonstrate-it-fires
